data.one_liner: OpenType text shaping for Dart and Flutter, returning glyph ids with offsets.
data.what_it_does: It runs HarfRust to perform GSUB substitutions and GPOS mark positioning, producing glyph ids, advances and offsets in font units. The API exposes a ShaperFont that can be registered, shaped, and disposed, and supports isolate attachment.
use_when: You need accurate mark positioning for scripts like Hebrew or Arabic.
You are generating PDFs or custom renderers that require glyph ids and positioning data.
You want to subset fonts for PDF by glyph id.
You need a pure Dart/Flutter solution without C/C++ dependencies.
avoid_when: You only need basic text rendering handled by Flutter’s Text widget.
You are targeting only Latin scripts without complex shaping.
You need a high-level layout engine that also handles line breaking and shaping together.
strengths: Pure Dart API with no C/C++ runtime; uses precompiled Rust library.
Supports isolate attachment and background shaping.
Provides glyph ids and offsets suitable for PDF and custom rendering.
Offers font subsetting by glyph id for PDFs.
weaknesses: Requires Rust toolchain if building from source; otherwise precompiled binaries needed.
No built-in line breaking or full layout engine; only shaping.
Limited to shaping; does not handle text layout or rendering.
Requires manual disposal of fonts and buffers.
data.setup_notes: Add dependency, run `flutter pub get`. If building from source, Rust must be installed. No special permissions. No build_runner needed.
